context:
Goal: no test-author agent is started just to reword a comment.
Problem (rule): the guard refuses every builder edit to a test file, per your ruling, so a comment fix costs a second agent.
Based on (ruling): your ruling of 2026-11-08 (decision builders-cannot-edit-tests): builders never write test content, and no override lifts it; this asks you to revisit it.
Based on (measured): Degen started a test-author agent only to reword comments on two of its pull requests.
The outcome your ruling protects is that a builder cannot weaken a test; comments cannot change what a test runs, and the language's own parser can prove a diff is comment-only.
Departs from: main refuses every builder test edit — option a allows a diff whose only changes are comments.
Why yours: it opens a path in your own ruling.
The retrospective recommends a, and thinks the widening label may be a false alarm: a comment-only allowance would hold in every repo, not bend the guard for one.

options.gain: Saves an agent per comment fix.
options.how: The guard tokenizes the old and new file and allows the edit only when nothing but comments changed.
options.label: Allow comment-only diffs, proven by the language's own tokenizer
options.lose: One more guard path to prove. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

ref: retrospective 21:53 CST Nov 12; Degen report plans/degen-report-2026-11-12.md
title: May a builder change only the comments in a test file?
why: It opens a path in your ruling that builders never edit tests.
